question: Should OpenClaw converge memory behavior around a new unified `memory.type`-style contract, the role-slot architecture in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504, or a docs/doctor clarification of the existing split surfaces?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, plugin ownership, memory write lifecycle, and migration behavior; source inspection proves the current split but cannot decide the product contract.

options.title: Sponsor role-slot plus migration contract
options.body: Use the role-slot direction as the canonical fix, but require docs, doctor migration, and explicit treatment of compaction memory flush and QMD/builtin semantics before closing this issue.

options.title: Add a smaller unified memory mode
options.body: Define a narrower `memory.type` or equivalent mode only if maintainers want one operator-facing knob over the current backend/flush/plugin surfaces.

options.title: Document current split as intentional
options.body: Keep the existing backend, slot, QMD, and flush surfaces but update docs/doctor to explain why team members can see different storage behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor role-slot plus migration contract
recommendation.body: Use the role-slot direction as the canonical fix, but require docs, doctor migration, and explicit treatment of compaction memory flush and QMD/builtin semantics before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the most direct recent history on the current memory config/runtime lines and the shipped per-agent SQLite fix.
